identity: Lethariel keeps the oldest trees in the Accord, and someone with a forged bough-seal is counting them for the axe.

quests.title: A Debt Beyond the Grave
quests.text: Even death has not persuaded the Debtbound Zombies to abandon their unpaid tolls. Lay six to rest at night in the {name:glades} {dir_of:lethariel:glades}, before their wandering feet ruin more saplings. Dawn will burn them, but I would sooner grant them peace than leave the matter to the sun.

quests.title: Before the Speeches Begin
quests.text: The Star Hall has requested a meal worthy of its deliberations; I should prefer one ready before they end. Bring me five pieces of Raw Meat and one Braided Sinew, hunting Moss-Antler Stags by day in the {name:glades} {dir_of:lethariel:glades} for the sinew. Their yellow names mean they will not attack first, so choose your quarry with care.

quests.title: No Charge for the Grass
quests.text: Someone has decided that walking beneath Lethariel's trees requires a fee, complete with an imitation of our bough-seal. Defeat four Toll Bandits after dark in the {name:glades} {dir_of:lethariel:glades}; they appear only at night and are few enough to require a patient search. We planted shade for travellers, not a source of revenue for thieves.

quests.title: The Missing Half of the Pie
quests.text: Ilwen Petalmeasure's berry deliveries keep shrinking, though her crate lists remain beautifully written. Visit her at Lorindor Berrycourt, following the road out into Lorindor, and ask what these tolls are costing us. One cannot bake the missing half of a pie from elegant handwriting.

quests.title: Bread Does Not Keep Star-Time
quests.text: Lethen Moonledger can predict a star's return but has missed a month's worth of bread collections. Speak with him at the Moonfall Observatory in Moonfall Wood and find out what keeps him from us. If he says he has been busy, remind him that dough rises without an appointment.

quests.title: What the Seal Was For
quests.text: Our bough-seal once meant that a tree would be tended; at the {name:poacher_camp} {dir_from_giver:poacher_camp}, it marks trees for the axe. Defeat five Unlicensed Poachers there, then {name:bough_counter_rusk}, who records the theft. They keep the camp by day and night; separate the leader from his guards before you face him. Some of those trees shaded the hands that first carved our seal.

quests.title: Where the Writ Wears Thin
quests.text: Rusk's reckoning reaches into the Glassroot Wilds, beyond the comfort of our walls. Report what you have learned to Faeris Rootbinder at Glassroot Gate. Those lands are contested, and the Accord's seal offers little shelter there; finish your training before you set out.

quests.title: Optional: A Forester's Path
quests.text: Our foresters know which roots will trip them; it is the teeth between the roots that trouble me. Kill six Redfang Vixens by day in the {name:greatwood} {dir_of:lethariel:greatwood}. They attack passing travellers, so tend to your wounds before seeking the next.

quests.title: Optional: The Last Collection
quests.text: A lord once claimed a tithe on this wood; he is long dead and his claim forgotten, yet the Tithe Revenants still come to collect. Lay six to rest at night in the {name:greatwood} {dir_of:lethariel:greatwood}. They endure more punishment than the Debtbound Zombies, so approach them prepared. Let this be the last service anyone performs in that lord's name.

quests.title: Optional: Streaks in the Glaze
quests.text: A councillor who overlooked a forged seal spent ten minutes discussing the streaks in my glaze. Bring me two Silver-Tip Fox Tails from Redfang Vixens in the {name:greatwood} {dir_of:lethariel:greatwood} by day, and I can replace my brushes. At least the vixens make their objections quickly.

quests.title: Bounty: Hunger Returns to Court
quests.text: We have recipes older than the Accord and a larder that never survives the week. Bring me eight pieces of Raw Meat here in Lethariel for payment. This supply order is repeatable; long life has done nothing to diminish anyone's appetite.
